title: Sign a PDF and Reply in the Same Email on iPhone
description: Save an email’s PDF to Files, sign a separate copy and attach the checked PDF to a reply in the original email thread on iPhone.
direct: Save the PDF attachment to Files, sign a separate copy, then attach that copy to a reply in the original email thread.
figureAlt: A paper form, a labeled signed copy and an envelope on a desk.
figureCaption: AI illustration of a signed copy going back to the original sender.
cards.decision.heading: Keep the source and signed copy easy to tell apart
cards.decision.body: Use the same folder for both files if that helps you find them. Give the new file a clear name such as Form-signed.pdf so you can select it with confidence in the reply.
sections.detail-1.heading: Check the attachment field
sections.detail-1.body: If the signed file is hard to find, open Files first and confirm its folder and name. Then return to the open reply. Avoid starting a new message from the PDF’s share sheet when the recipient expects a reply in the same thread. If Mail and Preview on your iPhone offer Apple’s direct PDF reply workflow, you can also return a signed copy through Preview.
sections.detail-2.heading: Follow the requested signing process
sections.detail-2.body: Space Sheep Studio develops PDF Compressor for iPhone. Its signing tool adds a visible mark. If the sender requires certificate signing or a specific portal, follow that process. Try any export tool once free. Further exports require Pro.

steps.step-1.text: Open the original email in Mail. Save the attached PDF to a folder you can find in Files. Leave the message in place.
steps.step-2.text: Open that PDF in PDF Compressor: Sign & Merge. If the recipient accepts a visible signature, use the signing tool and save a separate copy. Reopen it to check the signature and page count.
steps.step-3.text: Return to the original message and tap Reply. Use the attachment control to choose the signed PDF from Files. Check the filename and recipients before sending.
